from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
import pyspark
from pyspark.sql.functions import to_date, date_format
 
 
# Initialize Spark session
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("ReadCSVFile").getOrCreate()
 
# Read the CSV file from GCS
file_path = "s3a://syntasa-qa/qa/adhoc/puneet/spark_revamp/spark_revamp.csv"
#schedule = spark.read.csv(f"{file_path}", header=True, inferSchema=True)
 
df = spark.read \
    .option('delimiter', ',') \
    .option('header', True) \
    .csv(file_path)
 
##df = df.withColumn("time", date_format(to_date("time", "dd-MM-yyyy"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
 
#print(df)
#df = df.withColumn('date', current_date())
writeToEventStore(df, '@OutputTable1', 1,'time')

from pyspark.sql.functions import col, concat_ws, lit, row_number, lpad
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

# Step 1: Read input data
df = spark.sql("select * from @InputTable1 where time between @fromDate and @toDate")

# Step 2: Define a window partitioned by date (time) and ordered by any column (e.g., id or just keep as is)
window_spec = Window.partitionBy("time").orderBy(lit(1))  # or use orderBy("some_column") if needed

# Step 3: Add row number to each row per day
df_with_index = df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec) - 1)

# Step 4: Convert row number to hour string like "00", "01", etc.
df_with_hour = df_with_index.withColumn("hour_suffix", lpad(col("row_num").cast("string"), 2, "0"))

# Step 5: Append hour_suffix to time column
df_final = df_with_hour.withColumn("time", concat_ws("-", col("time"), col("hour_suffix"))).drop("row_num", "hour_suffix")

# Step 6: Show and write output
df_final.show(1000, truncate=False)

writeToEventStore(df_final, "@OutputTable1", 1, "time")

executionid = str(synutils.object.getAction().getExecutionId())
print(f"##### executionid: {executionid}")
